lines: A bank of six resonant band-pass filters tuned to the notes of a scale ring, excited by audio or by the module's own noise, with the level, resonance and tuning of each filter under separate control
The audio from the six filters, merged onto one, two or six channels of the cable as the output switch is set
Slews the V/OCT outputs so they glide from note to note instead of stepping; the lamp shows it is on
Locks that filter's tuning, so the NUDGE, P. V/OCT and TRSP. controls no longer move it; the lamp shows it locked
The note that filter is tuned to, a volt per octave with 0V for C4, running from -3.33V to 4.75V
The notes all six filters are tuned to, one channel of the cable each, a volt per octave with 0V for C4
Transposes that filter in whole semitones, an octave down to an octave up
An envelope following that filter's output, 0 to 10V, at the speed set by the envelope switch
Twelve channels: the six filters' envelopes on channels 1 to 6, and the level each filter is running at on channels 7 to 12, which reach 20V at full
The audio to be filtered; one channel on the cable feeds all six filters, two split them odd and even, three feed them in pairs, and six feed one filter each
Chooses the noise the module makes for itself while POLY IN is empty: brown, pink or white
Chooses how the six filters reach the output cable: MAIN merges all six onto channel 1, O/E puts the odd filters on channel 1 and the even ones on channel 2, and CH. gives each filter its own channel
Takes the envelope outputs from before the level controls instead of after them; the lamp shows the pre-fader setting
Sets what the envelope outputs carry: a fast follower, a slow follower, or a trigger
Sets the level of all six filters together, reaching twice unity gain at the top
Added to the global level knob, 5V adding the whole of the knob's range and -5V taking it away
Slews the level CV inputs, so a gate or a clock used as a level does not click
Sets that filter's level, silence at -5V and full at 5V, added to the matching channel of POLY LEVEL CV
Sets each filter's level from its own channel of the cable, silence at -5V and full at 5V, added to that filter's own level jack
Sets that filter's output level, silence at the bottom and full at the top
An indicator rather than a control: the module writes that filter's running output level into it every sample, so moving it has no effect
Takes that filter's resonance off the global control and onto its own knob and jacks; the lamp shows it is on its own
Sets that filter's resonance while its CH. Q lamp is lit, from a wide noisy band at the bottom to a narrow ringing sine at the top
Sets the resonance of every filter that is not on its own Q, from a wide noisy band at the bottom to a narrow ringing sine at the top
Added to the global Q knob, 10V adding the whole of its range and -10V taking it away
Added to that filter's own Q knob, 10V adding the whole of its range, and it does nothing until that filter's CH. Q lamp is lit
Adds to each filter's own Q knob from its own channel of the cable, and each channel does nothing until that filter's CH. Q lamp is lit
Chooses the filter all six channels use: 1P and 2P are the one-pass and two-pass MaxQ filters, and BP is the BpRe filter
Chooses the bank of scales to load; its name shows with an asterisk beside it until the LOAD button is pressed
Loads the bank chosen on the SELECT knob into the scale ring
Sets the gap between neighbouring filters, one note of the ring at the bottom and sixteen at the top, with the third filter staying where it is
Added to the spread knob, 10V adding the whole of its range
Slews the filters as they move from note to note, so they glide rather than jump
Added to the morph knob, 10V adding the whole of its range
Moves all six filters one note counter-clockwise around the ring
Moves all six filters one note clockwise around the ring
Rotates the filters around the ring, 0V leaving them where the buttons put them and 10V carrying them the whole way round
A rising edge moves all six filters one note counter-clockwise; it reads high above 1V
A rising edge moves all six filters one note clockwise; it reads high above 1V
Moves the ring to the previous scale of the bank
Moves the ring to the next scale of the bank
Chooses the scale within the bank, 0V for the first and 10V for the last
Makes a filter that passes the first note of a scale move on to the next scale, so rotating the notes walks through the whole bank
Chooses whether the odd-channel NUDGE knob, P. V/OCT jack and INV. LOCK button act on filter 1 alone or on filters 1, 3 and 5 together
Chooses whether the even-channel NUDGE knob, P. V/OCT jack and INV. LOCK button act on filter 6 alone or on filters 2, 4 and 6 together
Shifts the tuning of the odd filters by up to a semitone either way in the two MaxQ filter modes; in BP it slides them from their note towards the next note of the scale
Shifts the tuning of the even filters by up to a semitone either way in the two MaxQ filter modes; in BP it slides them from their note towards the next note of the scale
Shifts the odd filters' tuning by two volts to the octave in the MaxQ filter modes, not one; three channels on the cable tune filters 1, 3 and 5 separately
Shifts the even filters' tuning by two volts to the octave in the MaxQ filter modes, not one; three channels on the cable tune filters 2, 4 and 6 separately
Turns the lock on filter 1 round, and on filters 3 and 5 as well while the odd CH. SEL. switch is at 135
Turns the lock on filter 6 round, and on filters 2 and 4 as well while the even CH. SEL. switch is at 246
A rising edge turns the lock on filter 1 round, and on filters 3 and 5 as well while the odd CH. SEL. switch is at 135; it reads high above 1V
A rising edge turns the lock on filter 6 round, and on filters 2 and 4 as well while the even CH. SEL. switch is at 246; it reads high above 1V
Note — with nothing patched into POLY IN the module feeds the filters from its own noise, and a lamp lights to show the noise is in use
Note — click a light in the outer ring of the scale display to block that note, so no filter can tune to it; up to fourteen of the twenty can be blocked, and blocked notes are ringed in red
Note — the scale ring and the bank name are drawn rather than built from controls, so no click on them reaches this help
Note — the BpRe filter cannot use the user bank; choosing the two together puts the bank back to the last one that works with it
Note — a Spectrum module placed immediately to the right writes its own bank of scales into this module's user bank
Note — the audio output is clipped hard at ±5V for every channel, and a lamp lights when the input itself clips
Menu — CPU Mode: High (96Khz), Low (48KHz) (default) — sets the rate the filters run at, the higher one costing more processor time

Rainbow.notes: The P. V/OCT inputs are halved before use: Rainbow.cpp:716-717 multiplies the jack by 0.5 and clamps to plus or minus 5, and Tuning.cpp:64 and 76 raise two to that figure, so in the two MaxQ filter modes the jack needs 2V for an octave. The manual says the opposite, that the jack is 1V per octave with MaxQ and about 2V per octave with BpRe; the code wins, and this is why those two jacks are marked as plain CV rather than as pitch inputs. In the BpRe mode the same jack is added to the nudge knob's 0 to 4095 figure and divided by 4096 (Tuning.cpp:188 and 196), so it moves the filter by about a thousandth of the way to the next note and does almost nothing. The six level indicators beside the sliders are parameters with widgets, so they can be clicked and dragged, but Rainbow.cpp:768 writes the running output level into each of them every sample; moving one is undone in the same frame. Two more parameters, SLEWON and COMPRESS, are marked obsolete in the source and have no widget, and the fourth output, POLY_DEBUG, has no jack on the panel; none of the three can be clicked and none gets a line. Spread is the raw knob shifted right by eight and increased by one, giving whole-number gaps of 1 to 16 notes, with filter 3 as the fixed point (Rainbow.cpp:894 and Rotation.cpp:164). The channel level can reach 2, which is why channels 7 to 12 of POLY ENV reach 20V (Levels.cpp:62-68). Scale ring notes are blocked by clicking the ring display, which is a drawn widget rather than a parameter. The manual's tips say the audio output is not limited; Audio.cpp:115, 217-218 and 309 clamp every output sample to plus or minus 5V, so in this build it is.

lines: Expander for Rainbow that builds banks of user-defined scales and writes them into it; it goes immediately to the right of the Rainbow it feeds, and edits scales on its own wherever it is placed
Chooses which of the twenty-one notes of the scale is being edited
Chooses which of the eleven scales of the bank is being edited
Writes the whole bank of scales into the user bank of the Rainbow immediately to the left
Chooses how a note is worked out: HZ takes the frequency straight, ET calculates it from an equal temperament, and JI from whole-number ratios
Chooses whether CALC. sets the single note under the cursor or runs on through the bank setting many
Chooses whether a run of notes climbs by octaves or stacks the same interval over and over
Works out the note or notes from the settings, writes them into the scale and moves the cursor on
Chooses one of Rainbow's own banks to copy into this module for editing
Copies the bank chosen on SELECT into this module
The frequency of the note in hertz on the HZ page, the frequency of A4 the temperament is built on with ET, and the fundamental the ratios are taken from with JI
The octave the interval is counted from, on the ET and JI pages; it is unused on the HZ page
The number of intervals above the octave on the ET page, and the upper part of the interval's ratio on JI; it is unused on the HZ page
The lower part of the interval's ratio on the JI page; it is unused on the HZ and ET pages
How many slots to move on after each step of a calculation: 1 fills them in order, -1 works backwards, 2 skips one each time
How many equal parts the octave is divided into on the ET page, 12 being the usual; it is unused on the HZ and JI pages
Cents added to the frequency once it has been worked out, 1200 of them doubling it
An interval added before the calculation starts on the ET page, and the upper part of that starting offset's ratio on JI; it is unused on the HZ page
The lower part of the starting offset's ratio on the JI page; it is unused on the HZ and ET pages
How many notes a calculation writes, counting the first; 231 covers every note in the bank
Note — nothing reaches a Rainbow until the TRANSFER button is pressed, and then only if a Rainbow is immediately to the left and touching
Note — the ten figures on the right change their names and their meaning with the TYPE switch, and the ones that page does not use are greyed out
Note — a note on the display is cyan while it is as loaded, purple once it has been edited, and green once it has been transferred to a Rainbow
Note — the display of the bank and its frequencies is drawn rather than built from controls, so no click on it reaches this help
Note — no frequency above A10 is written, and a calculation that reaches it moves on without writing
Menu — Load Scala file — reads a Scala .scl file of intervals, ready to be applied
Menu — Apply Scala file — writes the intervals of the loaded Scala file into the bank, from the cursor to the end of it, on top of the base frequency the current page gives
RainbowScaleExpander.notes: A bank is eleven scales of twenty-one notes, 231 in all; the twenty-first note of each scale is the target the ring morphs towards rather than a note the filters sit on. The ten figures on the right are one parameter each (PARAMETER_PARAM 0 to 9) whose name, description and greying are rewritten when the TYPE switch changes page (RainbowExpander.cpp:439-558), which is why each of their lines has to cover three meanings. The maker's own descriptions for the JI page call Upper the denominator and Lower the numerator, which is the wrong way round against the manual and against the arithmetic. The module has no inputs and no outputs; everything reaches Rainbow through the expander connection, and only when TRANSFER is pressed. Frequencies are held between A0 at 13.75Hz and A10 at 28160Hz (RainbowExpander.cpp:258-259).

lines: One resonant band-pass filter of the kind Rainbow carries six of, with an envelope follower beside it
Sets the resonance, from a wide noisy band at the bottom to a narrow ringing sine at the top
Sets the filter frequency a volt per octave, ten octaves either side of C4 at 261.63Hz
Chooses the filter: 1P is the one-pass MaxQ filter and 2P the two-pass
Sets what the envelope output carries: a fast follower, a slow follower, or a trigger
Nothing in the module reads this switch: the noise it chooses is used only while the audio input is empty, and with that jack empty the module stops working altogether
Attenuates the frequency CV, from none of it at the bottom to all of it at the top
Attenuates the Q CV, from none of it at the bottom to all of it at the top
Raises the resonance, through its own attenuator, 10V for the whole range; a negative voltage does nothing
Shifts the filter frequency a volt per octave through its own attenuator, added to the frequency knob and held within ten octaves either side of C4
The audio to be filtered
The filtered audio
An envelope following the filter's output, 0 to 10V
Note — the module does nothing at all until a cable is in the audio input: with that jack empty it stops processing, and both outputs hold the last voltage they were given
Note — bypassing the module passes the audio input straight to the audio output

Droplet.notes: The NOISE switch is dead. Droplet.cpp:78 runs the whole of process only while the audio input is connected, and the noise DropletAudio.cpp:16-33 generates is reached only when that same jack is NOT connected, so the switch's value is passed to the audio code and never used. That also means the module is inert with the audio jack empty: no output is written at all, so both jacks hold whatever they last carried. The frequency jack is a true 1V per octave input, unlike Rainbow's P. V/OCT, which is halved. The filter type switch offers only the two MaxQ filters; the BpRe filter Rainbow has is not here. Droplet's audio output has no limiter: DropletAudio.cpp:76 writes the sample with no clamp, where Rainbow clamps its output to plus or minus 5V.
